Taking the natural logarithm of both sides and applying the laws of logarithms, we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}7\cdot {4}^{1-x} & <{3}^{x} \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡(7\cdot {4}^{1-x}) & <\operatorname{ln}⁡({3}^{x}) \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡7+(1-x)\operatorname{ln}⁡4 & <x\operatorname{ln}⁡3 \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡7+\operatorname{ln}⁡4-x\operatorname{ln}⁡4 & <x\operatorname{ln}⁡3 \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡4+\operatorname{ln}⁡7 & <x(\operatorname{ln}⁡3+\operatorname{ln}⁡4) \\ x & >\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡4+\operatorname{ln}⁡7}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3+\operatorname{ln}⁡4}\end{aligned}
$$
